text:
Jimmy Snuggerud has 13 goals in 23 games, and The Hockey News already has him on pace to be the Blues' first 40-goal scorer since Vladimir Tarasenko. The chances behind it are real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.7 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 96th percentile among forwards, and he sets up from behind the net far more than a typical forward does.

The finishing is the part to hold loosely. He has 13 goals on 6.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 25% after 12% last season, and the Blues have scored 8.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Our range for his true shooting tops out around 17%. Even so, our season projection runs from 28 to 43 goals, which tells you how good the underlying volume is for a 22-year-old.

What to watch: his ice time has slipped to 14 or 15 minutes in three of the last four games, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on last season (bottom 7% of forwards). The scoring is not the question. The other end is.
